B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Day AI says MCP requires a paid Agent tier; its product update says MCP is available from Turbo upward, with no usage-based MCP pricing. No separate MCP fee was found.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Pricing page lists Free at $0/month; Turbo at $24/month, Professional at $60/month, Executive at $200/month and Super at $800/month on annual billing. It also gives higher monthly prices and volume discounts for some plans.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Pricing is per deployed agent, not per seat or MCP call. The pricing page states annual prices are paid upfront and describes volume discounts. Tool availability depends on workspace plan and the selected agent; Free users in qualifying workspaces do not thereby gain MCP access.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: The selected agent tier controls available tools, models, and limits; data access follows workspace permissions. Day AI documents OAuth and workspace/assistant selection. Claude Team may require an administrator to enable the connector. The vendor states tier rate limits and quotas apply, without publishing specific MCP rate values on the reviewed pages.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor (plan and tier limits); workspace role/admin (data permissions and connector enablement); end user (OAuth consent and selected workspace/agent).

C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Protected-resource metadata names resource https://day.ai/api/mcp, authorization server https://day.ai, and bearer method header. Authorization-server metadata advertises authorization_code and refresh_token grants; response type code; PKCE S256; client_secret_post and client_secret_basic token authentication; revocation endpoint https://day.ai/api/oauth/revoke with client_secret_post, client_secret_basic, or none; and unauthenticated dynamic registration at https://day.ai/api/oauth/register. scopes_supported is exactly ["assistant:*:use", "sandboxes"]. D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official reference labels tools read-only or writes, sometimes “can overwrite”; it does not expose MCP annotation fields such as readOnlyHint or destructiveHint. 2. Documented server-side guards include duplicate-opportunity checks, a `confirm` parameter for bulk draft regeneration, and `confirmMajorContentReduction` for major page reductions. Other guidance is tool-description text. 3. OAuth scopes are `assistant:*:use` and `sandboxes`; docs say tools follow the selected agent tier and records follow the user's workspace role. Claude Team may require admin enablement. Metadata does not state token lifetime; SDK docs say about one hour and describe refresh. Revocation endpoint is advertised. 4. Tool inventory varies by plan and selected agent. No URL filter, readonly mode, or separate production/sandbox endpoint was found. A sandbox scope and sandbox file utilities are documented. 5. Day AI documents per-user email/calendar sharing controls and workspace permissions; no MCP-specific PII masking or field redaction was identified. 6. Tier API limits and quotas apply, but no concrete rate values were found. Tool-specific bounds include 1–25 person/org batch operations, up to 15 opportunity operations, search cursor pages up to 1,000 rows, and date enumeration capped at 400 days. 7. Tool schemas define expected inputs; docs describe safeguards and exact-match requirements. General unknown-argument rejection or systematic coercion was not found. 8. Vendor privacy materials promise continuous monitoring/logging and audit controls; MCP-specific call logging was not established. The tool list includes record/property history. 9. No rating/report/survey-to-vendor tool was found. `refine_campaign_drafting` accepts owner feedback to update drafting instructions; no vendor feedback purpose is stated. No MCP upsell response was verified. 10. `activate_skill`, `deactivate_skill`, and `manage_skills` expose persistent skill prompts and modes; instructions can shape agent behavior. `resolve_dates` says “ALWAYS use this tool instead of mental arithmetic”; search guidance directs schema lookup before non-trivial queries. 11. Workspace context, skills, campaign drafting settings and assistant instructions can persist and affect future agent behavior. 12. The documented inventory is a flat tool list, but tool access varies with the authorized agent/tier and skills can restrict available tools. 13. No arbitrary API, SQL, script, or code execution tool appears in the 78-tool official list. Sandbox export/upload helpers are listed, but they do not themselves execute code.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: ALWAYS use this tool instead of mental arithmetic for ANY weekday, relative-date, or timezone question
Before first querying an object type in a conversation, call read_crm_schema for that type
Only pass allowDuplicate: true after the user confirms this is a separate deal.
Pass true ONLY after the user has seen the exact draft count from a previous call of this tool and explicitly confirmed the regeneration.
The MCP server will handle OAuth authentication automatically when your client connects for the first time.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The reference describes one endpoint whose available tool inventory depends on the workspace plan and selected agent; skill activation can also switch modes with restricted tools and a specific prompt.

The official reference includes tool schemas. No catalogue-only tools were added because the official reference supplies a current inventory. Third-party snapshots differ: MartechDB reports 42 tools on 2026-10-27; Claude's directory shows 25; Agentman describes an older 42-tool list. These snapshots are not substituted for the official list. The action file contains all 78 official names; its parameter field points to the official schema rather than duplicating every schema.

E_aggregated.token_method: Could not compute from an initialize response: no exact initialize instructions/tool-definition payload was available locally. The official tool reference is available as a web page but the complete serialized payload could not be measured from the supplied evidence.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The documented MCP email tool creates or updates drafts; the reviewed official tool list does not include a tool to send email through a mail thread. Day AI's software privacy policy describes connected Gmail capabilities that include sending mail, so this is a difference between the documented MCP tool surface and the broader product. The product also offers UI settings and workflows beyond the listed MCP operations; no full UI-to-tool parity inventory was found.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The tool reference advises agents to call `read_crm_schema` before non-trivial queries and to use `resolve_dates` for date reasoning. Descriptions also prescribe pagination, source-date anchoring, and user confirmation. These are text instructions except where a specific tool parameter or server validation is documented.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Day AI says MCP access follows agent-tier and workspace-role permissions and that changes are tracked and audited. Its privacy policy says it does not use Customer Platform Data to train models, does not share that data with advertising partners, and promises notice of qualifying security incidents within 72 hours. It describes customer data retention during subscription and deletion timelines after request or termination.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The MCP page describes OAuth authentication, token refresh, and user revocation from workspace settings. It says tokens are stored locally and not transmitted to third parties. The privacy policy describes encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, and subprocessors bound by data-protection terms.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth metadata supports the advertised protected-resource authorization flow and exposes scopes, registration, PKCE, and revocation. Tool descriptions document some explicit guards, but the public hosted-server implementation is unavailable, so most permission, audit, retention, and data-protection statements could not be verified as MCP request-handler behavior. The general privacy-policy promises apply to the service and customer data, not specifically to a particular MCP call.

contradictions: The supplied endpoint prefetch reports an unauthenticated POST to https://day.ai/api/mcp returning HTTP 200 with `Invalid Request: Request body is missing`; the input's connection-test evidence says HTTP 401. The available evidence therefore shows different request/response conditions, and the supplied POST response has no WWW-Authenticate header.

The official tool reference generated 2026-10-07 names 78 tools for a Professional agent. MartechDB reports 42 tools on 2026-10-27, and Anthropic's directory lists 25. These third-party inventories differ from the newer official reference and from one another.
Day AI's MCP page says a paid Agent tier is required, while product updates state MCP is available from Turbo upward. No Free-tier MCP access was established from the official current tool reference.
observations_for_research: The official tool reference itself is generated from the hosted endpoint and identifies a dated plan-specific inventory, while noting that tools/list is authoritative for each authorized client.
The authorization server's broad assistant-use scope does not expose separate scopes for reading, writing, email, campaigns, or other tool categories.
Some tool descriptions contain detailed safeguards and procedural instructions, while explicit server-enforced controls are only documented for particular operations and parameters.
The server exposes persistent agent behavior controls through workspace instructions, assistant settings, and skill management tools.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, pages/, and available local code first. The public day-ai-sdk repository is an MIT TypeScript client with examples, not the hosted endpoint implementation; the SDK local copy was unavailable because the repository fetch was incomplete, so a commit hash could not be verified. The separate gtm-brain repository was not treated as endpoint code. Checked official MCP, pricing, update, legal, privacy, trust, SDK, generated tool-reference, and schema pages, plus Claude, MartechDB, MCP.so, and Agentman listings. MCP.so had no tool list. Agentman/Claude/MartechDB are third-party snapshots and were not used to replace official tool names. The complete 78-name official inventory is in actions.json; published parameter schemas are linked there but not duplicated in that file.
